localBiteReport: Fall inshore fishing on Choctawhatchee Bay is in solid form heading into early November, with water temperature at 76°F. Redfish remain the top bay target: fish in the 25–26-inch range are holding around bridge structure and responding well to a variety of natural baits including pinfish, croakers, spot minnows, and herring, with heavier weights needed on stronger tidal flow. Speckled trout in the 22–27-inch class are also active and closely tied to bait concentrations — finding the right bait school is key to consistent catches, with live bait leading the way and artificials in deeper water expected to improve as conditions cool further into fall. The most recent Choctawhatchee Bay flats-specific report (week of Oct 23–29) noted that redfish up to about 23 inches are still holding in guts, potholes, and shallow feeding areas despite recent storm disruption, with visibility good enough for sight fishing; after a cold front passage, cut natural bait outperformed both artificials and live greenies on the flats.
